metadata.name: traceroute
metadata.displayName: traceroute - Print route packets take to a host
metadata.description: Trace the path packets take to a network host

installation.note: On some Ubuntu systems traceroute is in the inetutils-traceroute or traceroute package

overview.summary: traceroute shows the path that packets take from your machine to a destination host. It displays each hop (router) along the way and round-trip times, helping identify where latency or packet loss occurs.
when_to_use: Diagnose network connectivity or latency issues
See which routers packets pass through to a host
Identify where a path fails or becomes slow

syntax.description: HOST can be a hostname or IP address. Options control probe count, timeout, and display.

options.description: Do not resolve IP addresses to hostnames (faster, less DNS dependency)
options.use_case: When you want quicker output or DNS is slow/unavailable

options.description: Maximum number of hops to probe (default often 30)
Time to wait for a response (seconds)
options.use_case: Adjust timeout on slow or lossy paths

examples.title: Trace route to a host
examples.description: Show each hop and RTT to example.com

examples.title: Trace without DNS lookups
examples.description: Trace to Google DNS showing only IPs
examples.use_case: Faster output, useful when DNS is slow
